title: Configure and verify Layer 2 discovery protocols

questions.question: Which protocol is an IEEE standard that collects information from neighboring devices on their identity and capabilities?
questions.explanation: LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB and provides standards-based neighbor discovery.

correct.explanation: LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB and provides standards-based neighbor discovery.

incorrect.explanation: CDP is Cisco proprietary — the stem asks for an IEEE standard protocol for neighbor identity and capabilities, which is LLDP (802.1AB), not CDP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Picking Cisco-only CDP for IEEE standard requirement
incorrect.whatItDoes: CDP describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given LLDP is IEEE 802, LLDP matches the tested behavior — CDP applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1b is not the IEEE neighbor discovery standard — LLDP is defined in IEEE 802.1AB for collecting neighbor device information.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting nonexistent 802.1b as discovery standard
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1b describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given LLDP is IEEE 802, LLDP matches the tested behavior — 802.1b applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1a is not LLDP — IEEE 802.1AB defines Link Layer Discovery Protocol for standards-based neighbor information exchange.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing 802.1a with 802.1AB LLDP standard
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1a describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given LLDP is IEEE 802, LLDP matches the tested behavior — 802.1a applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: IEEE neighbor discovery standard → LLDP (802.1AB), not Cisco CDP.

questions.question: How often are CDP frames sent out of the device by default?

answerReview.examTip: CDP defaults: timer 60 s, hold-time 180 s — do not swap them.
